articles.full_content:
Pune, 6 th November 2026
The National Statistics Office (NSO), Field Operations Division (FOD), Sub-Regional Office, Solapur, under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), is actively conducting a wide spectrum of socio-economic, industrial, and price-related surveys across the region. These nationwide surveys are pivotal in shaping national economic policies, calculating key indicators like GDP and inflation, evaluating employment trends, and assessing rural and urban socio-economic conditions. Below is an overview of the key ongoing survey operations undertaken by NSO SRO Solapur.

Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, successfully concludes Special Campaign 6 for institutionalising Swachhata and reducing pendency
articles.full_content:
The Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG), Government of India, has issued guidelines vide Office Memorandum No. Q-11/01/2026-O&M (e-10171) dated 13.08.2026 for the implementation of Special Campaign 6 from 2 October to 31 October 2026 . The campaign aims to institutionalize Swachhata (cleanliness), optimize workspace utilization, reduce pendency and enhance administrative efficiency across Government offices.
In line with these objectives, the Department of Revenue (DoR) undertook focused initiatives to promote cleanliness, improve workplace efficiency, ensure systematic record management, facilitate e-waste disposal, reduce pendency and strengthen citizen-centric service delivery. These efforts reaffirm the Department ’ s commitment to transparent, responsive and accountable governance.
As part of Special Campaign 6, a cleanliness drive was conducted at the lawns near India Gate and within office premises. The Department has also made significant progress in reducing pendency and improving record management. Approximately 400 files were weeded out or closed, around 1836 public grievances were disposed of, and 5 references received from the Prime Minister ’ s Office (PMO) were addressed. Furthermore, revenue amounting to approximately ₹6,00,000/- was generated up to 31 October 2026 through campaign-related activities such as e-waste disposal & scrap disposal.
Special Campaign 6 extends beyond cleanliness to encompass the broader goals of administrative reform. Through the systematic decluttering of office spaces and processes, improved records management, timely disposal of pending matters and enhanced accountability, the Department of Revenue is working towards a more efficient, responsive and citizen-centric administrative ecosystem.
The Department remains committed to sustaining these initiatives and embedding the principles of Swachhata, efficiency and good governance into its day-to-day functioning.
articles.summary: The Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG), Government of India, has issued guidelines vide Office Memorandum No. Q-11/01/2026-O&M (e-10171) dated 13.08.2026 for the implementation of Special Campaign 6 from 2 October to 31 October 2026 . The campaign aims to institutionalize Swachhata (cleanliness), optimize workspace utilization, reduce pendency and enhance administrative efficiency across Government offices.

articles.title: Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser and DPIIT Launches API Integration between Startup India and I-STEM Portals to Strengthen Access to National Research Infrastructure
articles.full_content:
The Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India, in collaboration with the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, launched the API integration of DPIIT’s Startup India Portal with the Indian Science, Technology and Engineering Facilities Map (I-STEM) Portal on 6 November 2026, under the chairmanship of Prof. Ajay Kumar Sood, Principal Scientific Adviser (PSA). The initiative seeks to strengthen linkages between the startup ecosystem and the country’s research infrastructure by enabling DPIIT-recognised startups to discover and access existing scientific and testing facilities.
The launch was attended by Dr. (Mrs.) Parvinder Maini, Scientific Secretary, Office of the PSA; and Shri Ateesh Kumar Singh, Additional Secretary, DPIIT. Dr. Vishal Choudhary, Scientist-F; Dr. Santhosh Nair, Scientist-D; Dr. Shefali Uttam, Technical Staff, Office of the PSA; and members of the DPIIT and I-STEM teams were also present. Dr. Vishal Choudhary gave a brief presentation about the current status and impact of I-STEM.
Speaking on the occasion, Prof. Sood highlighted that the integration represents an institutional convergence beyond a digital interface, connecting startup requirements with the scientific infrastructure and technical capabilities available across the country. He emphasised its potential to lower R&D costs, avoid duplication of capital-intensive facilities and enhance the utilisation of publicly funded infrastructure. He also underscored the importance of stronger industry–academia linkages and access to specialised facilities for deep-tech startups across technology development, prototyping, testing and validation.
Dr. Maini highlighted I-STEM’s role in promoting the sharing and optimal utilisation of scientific infrastructure across academic and research institutions. She noted that the integration would simplify the discovery of relevant facilities for DPIIT-recognised startups, helping address infrastructure-related barriers to technology development and innovation.
Shri Ateesh Kumar Singh highlighted the role of the integration in strengthening DPIIT’s efforts to build an enabling environment for startups, particularly in the deep-tech sector. He noted that the integration would provide DPIIT-recognised startups with improved visibility of specialised research, testing and prototyping facilities, enabling them to identify suitable infrastructure, reduce the need for independent capital investment in expensive equipment, and access institutional capabilities to support product development, testing and technology validation.
The integration will facilitate seamless, API-enabled interoperability between the Startup India Portal and I-STEM, with the proposed incorporation of Single Sign-On (SSO) functionality in subsequent phases, enabling DPIIT-recognised startups to directly access and leverage I-STEM's scientific infrastructure and research facilities through t

Department of Financial Services Conferred with the ‘PM Surya Ghar Excellence Award’ for Leading Government Building Solarisation
articles.full_content:
DFS achieves 100% saturation across all feasible administrative buildings, commissioning 61.50 MW rooftop solar capacity across 2,576 sites Award presented by the Vice-President of India at the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo 2026, Bharat Mandapam
Demonstrating an exceptional institutional commitment towards this national mandate, the Department of Financial Services has successfully achieved 100% solarisation across all identified feasible buildings of organisations under its administrative control. Out of 4,144 buildings, after technical and structural feasibility assessments—accounting for roof-access rights, building ownership, shadow profiles and load-bearing parameters—2,576 viable buildings were identified for solarization. Organisations of DFS has fully commissioned rooftop solar PV plants across all 2,576 feasible buildings, delivering an aggregate installed clean capacity of 61.50 MW.
In view of the above significant achievement Department of Financial Services it was conferred with the PM Surya Ghar Excellence Award (2 nd Position) under the category “ Maximum Buildings Solarized by Central Ministries/Departments ” on 05.11.2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi.
The award was presented by the Vice-President of India during the PM Surya Ghar Excellence Awards Ceremony, during the valedictory session of Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo 2026 (BRE Summit). The summit was organised by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) alongside the 9 th General Assembly of the International Solar Alliance (ISA) and the 4th International Conference on Green Hydrogen (ICGH).
The conferment of the PM Surya Ghar Excellence Award underscores the Department of Financial Services’ steadfast contribution towards India’s broader net-zero commitments and reinforces the proactive role of financial institutions in driving sustainable development through infrastructure.

CAQM invokes Stage-III of GRAP in Delhi-NCR with immediate effect as Delhi records an AQI of 382
articles.full_content:
The Sub-Committee on GRAP in its meeting held on 6th November 2026 comprehensively reviewed the air quality scenario in the Delhi-NCR region, along with the IMD/IITM forecasts. Delhi recorded a daily average Air Quality Index (AQI) of 382 i.e. ‘Very Poor’ category, as per the daily AQI Bulletin provided by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) on 6th November 2026, due to poor dispersion of pollutants on account of unfavourable meteorological conditions, as observed by the sub-committee. Also, IMD/IITM forecasts indicated that the AQI was likely to slip into the ‘Severe’ category in the coming days.
In an effort to prevent further deterioration of air quality, the CAQM Sub-Committee on GRAP has taken the call to invoke the action plan as per Stage-III of the extant GRAP in the entire NCR. All actions as envisaged under Stage-III of the extant GRAP, are required to be implemented with immediate effect in right earnest by all the agencies concerned in NCR, in addition to all Stage- I and Stage-II actions of GRAP already in force. Further, agencies responsible for implementing measures under GRAP including Pollution Control Boards (PCBs) of NCR States and DPCC have been advised to ensure strict implementation of actions under all three stages of the GRAP, during this period.
The action plan includes steps to be implemented/ ensured by various agencies including Pollution Control Boards of NCR States and DPCC. The Sub-Committee has urged citizens to adhere to the following specific steps listed in Citizen Charter of Stage-III along with Stage-I and Stage-II of GRAP and assist in effective implementation of the under:
• Walk or use cycles for small distances.
Walk or use cycles for small distances.
• Choose a cleaner transport mode to commute.
Choose a cleaner transport mode to commute.
• Combine short journeys and reduce trips.
Combine short journeys and reduce trips.
• Postpone private gatherings that increase traffic and outdoor exposure.
Postpone private gatherings that increase traffic and outdoor exposure.
• Do not use coal and wood for heating purpose.
Do not use coal and wood for heating purpose.
• House owners may also provide electric heaters to security/other staff employed by them to avoid open burning of biomass / wood / MSW.
House owners may also provide electric heaters to security/other staff employed by them to avoid open burning of biomass / wood / MSW.
• Follow hybrid mode for primary schools and work-from-home when instructed.
Follow hybrid mode for primary schools and work-from-home when instructed.
The Commission is closely monitoring the situation and will review the air quality scenario on a regular basis in the coming days. The extant GRAP order is available on the Commission’s official website and may be accessed on the given link: https://caqm.nic.in/FileUploadDomain/WebsiteDocument/GRAP/GRAP%20Orders/e93ab81c-af66-4c41-a6b1-41bdd4a8ff28.pdf .
